Sean: Irish form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'.
Soufian: French spelling of Arabic Sufyan, from sufyan, perhaps 'swift' or 'one who sails freely'.
Adriaan: Dutch form of Adrian, from Latin Hadrianus, 'man from Hadria' (Adriatic).
Nawfel: Maghrebi spelling of Arabic Nawfal, meaning 'generous' or 'sea', or 'giver'.
Luigi: Italian form of Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Maura: Latin, 'dark-skinned' or 'Moorish'; also an Irish form meaning 'great' or from Mary.
Edwin: English, from Old English ead 'wealth' and wine 'friend', 'rich friend'.
Teun: Dutch short form of Antonius (Anton), from the Roman family name Antonius.
Ilyass: Maghrebi spelling of Arabic Ilyas, the Quranic form of Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Yoan: French and Bulgarian form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Joaquim: Portuguese and Catalan form of Joachim, Hebrew 'God will establish'.
Wiktoria: Polish form of Victoria, from Latin victoria, 'victory'.
Alper: Turkish, from alp 'hero' and er 'man', 'brave warrior'.
Yuri: Russian form of George, Greek 'farmer'. In Japanese a girls' name meaning 'lily'.
Aloys: French and German form of Aloysius, a Latinised form of Louis, Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Adelin: French, from Germanic adal 'noble'; masculine of Adeline.
Caitlyn: English variant of Caitlin, the Irish form of Catherine, probably Greek 'pure'.
Jos: Dutch short form of Joseph, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Simone: French and Italian form of Simon (masculine in Italian, feminine in French), Hebrew 'he has heard'.
Fem: Dutch short form of Femke, a Frisian diminutive of Fem (Femme), from Germanic 'woman' or 'maiden'. Origin uncertain.
Liah: Variant of Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'cow'. Biblical wife of Jacob.
Ioan: Romanian and Welsh form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Hadi: Arabic, 'guide' or 'leader to the right path', one of the attributes of God.
Gustav: Scandinavian and German, probably from Old Norse 'staff of the Goths'.
Ariel: Hebrew, 'lion of God'. A spirit in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
Aysima: Turkish, probably from ay 'moon' and sima 'face', 'moon-faced'.
Cayden: Modern American variant of Caden, perhaps from Welsh cadaw 'battle' or Arabic 'companion'. Origin uncertain.
Amna: Arabic, meaning 'peace, safety, tranquillity'. Mother of Muhammad was Amina.
Eleonor: Variant of Eleanor, of uncertain origin; possibly Provençal Aliénor or a form of Helen.
Saverio: Italian form of Xavier, from the Basque place name Etxeberri, 'new house'.
Izia: Polish short form of Izabela or a modern coinage, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Origin uncertain.
Lamar: French, from 'de la mer', 'of the sea'; also a Germanic surname and Arabic-influenced use.
Arsen: Armenian and Russian form of Arsenios, from Greek arsen, 'masculine, virile'.
Halid: Bosnian and Turkish form of Arabic Khalid, 'eternal, immortal'.
Bes: Probably the Egyptian god Bes, a protective dwarf deity; or a pet form. Origin uncertain.
Marielou: French compound of Marie and Louise; Marie from Hebrew Miryam, Louise from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Willy: Pet form of William, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet', 'resolute protector'.
Nayeli: Zapotec (Mexican), 'I love you', from Nayeli. Also Nahuatl in popular use.
Lux: Latin, 'light'. Used as a modern given name.
Zelda: Yiddish short form of Griselda, Germanic 'grey battle'; also Yiddish 'happy, blessed'.
Telio: Probably a modern variant of Italian Tellio or a short form of names ending in -telio. Origin uncertain.
Mouhamadou: West African (Wolof, Fula) form of Muhammad, Arabic 'praiseworthy'.
Yüsra: Turkish form of Arabic Yusra, 'ease' or 'prosperity'.
Evana: Probably a feminine form of Evan (Welsh John) or a variant of Ivana. Origin uncertain.
Moesa: Dutch and Arabic variant of Musa, the Quranic form of Moses, possibly Egyptian 'son, child'.
Nea: Greek, 'new'. Also Finnish name of uncertain origin.
Luay: Arabic, Luayy, a diminutive of lu'a 'bull', or 'brightness'. Name of an ancestor of the Quraysh.
Petru: Romanian form of Peter, from Greek petros, 'rock'.
Mirha: Probably a variant of Mirra or Mirha; Arabic 'joy' or from myrrh. Origin uncertain.
Mylana: Modern coined name, probably a blend of Mila or Milana with Lana. Origin uncertain.
Torvi: Probably a Norse-inspired name, from Old Norse Þorvi, 'Thor' element. Origin uncertain.
Émy: French form of Emmy, from Emma or Amy; Emma is Germanic 'whole, universal'; Amy is French 'beloved'.
Yakout: Arabic Yaqut, 'ruby' or 'hyacinth', a precious gem.
Deen: Arabic din, 'religion, faith'. Also Dutch pet form of Deen, meaning 'Dane'.
Kleo: Greek, from Kleio (Clio), 'to make famous', the muse of history.
Rumi: Persian, 'from Rum' (Anatolia). The 13th-century poet Jalal ad-Din Rumi. Japanese Rumi also exists.
Troi: Probably from Troy, English from Troyes in France; or a Star Trek character name. Origin uncertain.
Sofiia: Ukrainian transliteration of Sofia, from Greek sophia, 'wisdom'.
Léas: Probably a modern French variant of Léa or Léo, with Hebrew or Latin roots. Origin uncertain.
Ossaid: Probably a variant of Arabic Usayd or Asid, 'little lion'. Origin uncertain.
Jarne: Flemish, probably from the Scandinavian name Jarne or Jarn, or a short form of Jaron. Origin uncertain.
Ellen: English and Scandinavian form of Helen, Greek 'torch' or 'bright one'.
Lies: Dutch short form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Jimmy: English pet form of James, from Hebrew Yaakov (Jacob), 'supplanter'.
Maïté: Basque form of Maite, from Spanish and Basque 'beloved'. Also a form of Marie.
Samia: Arabic, 'elevated, exalted' or 'high'. Also a form of Sami.
Philippe: French form of Philip, from Greek philippos, 'lover of horses'.
Christina: From Latin christianus, 'follower of Christ'. Feminine of Christian.
Sandra: Short form of Alessandra, the Italian feminine of Alexander, Greek 'defender of men'.
Rhune: Probably a modern variant of Rune, from Old Norse run 'secret lore' or from the Basque La Rhune mountain. Origin uncertain.
Alexy: Variant of Alexis, from Greek alexo, 'to defend, help'.
Yinthe: Flemish modern coined name, possibly from Ingrid or Yinte. Origin uncertain.
Kaylee: Modern American invented name, perhaps from Kayla or Kelly with the -lee ending. Origin uncertain.
Benoit: French form of Benedict, from Latin benedictus, 'blessed'.
Lohan: Probably Breton or Irish variant of Lohan; may relate to Gaelic 'lohan'. Origin uncertain.
Kendra: English, probably from Old English 'knowledge' or a feminine form of Kenneth. Origin uncertain.
Maren: Scandinavian and German, a form of Margaret or Marina; Latin marinus 'of the sea'.
Halil: Turkish form of Arabic Khalil, 'close friend'.
Neil: Irish and Scottish, from Gaelic Niall, perhaps 'champion' or 'cloud'.
Virgile: French form of Virgil, from Latin Vergilius, a Roman family name of uncertain origin.
Zaineb: Variant of Arabic Zaynab, a fragrant tree or 'adornment of the father'.
Tijn: Dutch short form of Martijn or Valentijn, or from Constantijn. Martin is Latin 'of Mars'.
Linn: Scandinavian, from Linnea, the twinflower named after Carl Linnaeus; also Old English 'waterfall'.
Etienne: French form of Stephen, from Greek stephanos, 'crown, garland'.
Viktoria: German and Scandinavian form of Victoria, Latin 'victory'.
Cécilia: Latin and French, a feminine form of Cecil from Latin caecus 'blind'. Saint Cecilia patron of music.
Dan: Hebrew, 'he judged'; also a short form of Daniel. A biblical son of Jacob.
Ella-Marie: Compound of Ella (Germanic 'all' or a short form of Eleanor) and Marie (Hebrew Miryam).
Mirac: Turkish form of Arabic Miraj, 'ascent' or 'ladder', Muhammad's night journey.
Midas: Greek, a legendary king of Phrygia with the golden touch; the name is probably of Phrygian origin.
Jolie: French, 'pretty'. Also used as an English given name.
Nilay: Turkish, 'moon-like' or 'blue' from Persian nil 'blue'; of uncertain exact derivation.
Orlando: Italian form of Roland, from Germanic 'fame of the land'.
Beatriz: Spanish and Portuguese form of Beatrice, from Latin beatrix 'she who brings happiness'.
Eloi: French from Latin Eligius, 'chosen'. Saint Eligius was a goldsmith bishop.
Raquel: Spanish and Portuguese form of Rachel, Hebrew 'ewe'.
Asmin: Probably a variant of Yasmin or Asmina, from Persian 'jasmine'. Origin uncertain.
Rosario: Spanish and Italian, from Latin rosarium, 'rose garden'; the Marian rosary.
Cruz: Spanish and Portuguese, 'cross'. Also a surname.
Léah: French form of Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'cow'.
Jon: Short form of Jonathan or Scandinavian/Basque form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Albin: French, German and Polish from Latin Albinus, 'white' or 'fair'.
Gaia: Greek, 'earth'. Gaia was the primordial earth goddess.
Nikita: Russian male name from Greek Niketas, 'victor'. In India a feminine name.
Elyesa: Modern variant of Arabic Ilyas or Elijah. Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'; spelling uncertain.
Art: Short form of Arthur, from Welsh artos 'bear' or Celtic; also Irish Art meaning 'bear'.
Luciana: Italian and Portuguese feminine of Luciano, from Latin lux 'light'.
Elion: Probably a Welsh or Breton variant of Elian, or Hebrew 'Elyon' meaning 'highest'. Origin uncertain.
Raisa: Russian and Yiddish, from Greek 'easygoing' or Arabic 'leader'; also Yiddish for 'rose'.
Lucio: Italian and Spanish form of Lucius, from Latin lux, 'light'.
Ania: Polish pet form of Anna, Hebrew 'grace'.
Nyla: Modern name, perhaps from Arabic Nayla 'one who attains' or from the Nile. Origin uncertain.
Kelya: Modern coined name, probably a blend of Kelly and Kaya. Origin uncertain.
Kaylan: Modern invented name, probably a variant of Kayla or Kalan. Origin uncertain.
Kinan: Arabic, Kinana, a tribe name of the Quraysh; also Arabic 'quiver'.
Ayda: Turkish form of Arabic Aida, 'visitor' or 'returning'. Also Persian 'bright'.
Maysae: Arabic Maysa, 'proud walk' or 'stately gait', from maysa, a type of tree.
Maïna: Breton, a variant of Maëlle or Maina; possibly Native American Algonquin 'strong'. Origin uncertain.
Keziah: Hebrew, 'cassia', a spice tree. A daughter of Job in the Bible.
Arvin: Persian and Germanic; Persian 'river' or Old English 'friend of the people'. Origin varies.
Cassiopée: French form of Cassiopeia, a mythological queen and constellation; Greek origin of uncertain meaning.
Isla: Scottish, from the Hebridean island Islay; popular English given name.
Josie: English pet form of Josephine, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Gerard: Germanic, from ger 'spear' and hard 'brave', 'brave with the spear'.
Isaï: French form of Jesse, father of King David, Hebrew possibly 'gift'.
Lilian: English, from lily or a variant of Elizabeth. Also male in French.
Nesta: Welsh, pet form of Agnes, Greek hagne 'pure'.
Isak: Scandinavian form of Isaac, Hebrew 'he laughs'.
Ary: Dutch short form of Adriaan or Arie; also Hebrew 'lion'.
Raphaelle: French feminine of Raphael, Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Bora: Turkish, 'storm'; also Albanian and Slavic 'snow', and a name of various origins.
Lilio: Italian, from Latin lilium, 'lily'. Also a form of Lilian.
Amaro: Spanish and Portuguese, from a Basque or Latin source, 'bitter' or 'dark'. Also Saint Amaro.
Kaia: Variant of Kaja; used in Scandinavia, Hawaiian 'sea' and Greek 'earth'. Origin varies.
Nori: Japanese, 'law' or 'principle', used in many given names.
Ézéchiel: French form of Ezekiel, Hebrew 'God strengthens'.
Thilo: German short form of Theodolf or Dietrich, Germanic 'people' elements.
Medard: French, Germanic, from magan 'might' and hard 'brave', 'strong and brave'. Saint Medard.
Yris: Probably a variant of Iris, Greek 'rainbow'.
Ozzy: English pet form of Oswald, Old English 'divine power', or Osbourne.
Cezanne: French surname from Cézanne, the painter; probably from a Provençal place name. Used as a given name.
Liselle: Modern coined name, blending Lise or Elise with Gisèle or Danielle. Origin uncertain.
Rho: The Greek letter. Probably chosen as a short, modern name. Origin uncertain.
Élya: Probably a French modern variant of Élia, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Origin uncertain.
Élio: French and Italian, from Latin Aelius, a Roman family name, or Greek 'sun'.
Mencia: Spanish, from medieval Menda or Mencía, perhaps Germanic or Latin, uncertain meaning.
Keano: Modern name, possibly a variant of Keanu, Hawaiian 'cool breeze', or Irish Cian. Origin uncertain.
Wesley: English surname from Old English 'west meadow', used as a given name.
Mirte: Dutch, 'myrtle', the evergreen shrub; Greek myrtos.
Bradley: English surname from Old English 'broad clearing'.
Tania: Russian pet form of Tatiana, from the Roman Tatius.
Angel: From Greek angelos, 'messenger'. Used for both sexes; Spanish masculine form.
Storm: English and Scandinavian, 'storm', from the weather phenomenon.
Sinan: Turkish and Arabic, 'spear point'; the architect Mimar Sinan.
Séléna: French form of Selena, Greek selene, 'moon'.
Hüseyin: Turkish form of Arabic Husayn, a diminutive of hasan, 'good, handsome'.
Kacper: Polish form of Caspar (Gaspard), perhaps Persian 'treasurer'. One of the Magi.
Manuela: Spanish and Portuguese feminine of Manuel, from Emmanuel, Hebrew 'God is with us'.
Mohamed-Amine: Arabic compound, Muhammad 'praiseworthy' and Amin 'trustworthy, faithful'.
Jim: English pet form of James, from Hebrew Jacob, 'supplanter'.
Lenne: Probably a Dutch variant of Lena or Leen, from Helena or Magdalena. Origin uncertain.
Elona: Probably a variant of Elena or Elon; Greek 'bright, torch' or Hebrew 'oak'. Origin uncertain.
Lee: English, from Old English 'woodland clearing' or 'meadow'. Also used in Chinese and Korean as a surname.
Nine: Probably a Dutch pet form of Catharina or Anne, or from Nina. Origin uncertain.
Erica: Latin 'heather', or the feminine of Eric, Old Norse 'ever ruler'.
Danny: English pet form of Daniel, Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Améline: French, a variant of Amelia or Emeline, from Germanic amal 'work' or 'industrious'.
Marianne: French, a compound of Marie and Anne; Hebrew Miryam and Channah, 'grace'.
Jaden: Modern American, possibly a variant of Jadon, from Hebrew 'he has judged' or 'thankful'.
Dila: Turkish, meaning 'heart'; also a Kurdish name.
Szymon: Polish form of Simon, Hebrew 'he has heard'.
Emie: Pet form of Emilie or Emma, Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Gaetano: Italian, 'from Gaeta', a town in Lazio. Saint Cajetan.
